title: Grade 8 Science — Mon, Jun 09
description: Metals and Non-metals — Day 1 of 5: Physical properties
subject: science

questions.question: Which property describes the ability of a metal to be beaten into thin sheets?
questions.explanation: Malleability is the property that allows metals to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets (e.g., gold foil, aluminium foil).

questions.question: The ability of a metal to be drawn into thin wires is called:
questions.explanation: Ductility allows metals like copper and gold to be drawn into long thin wires. Copper wires are used in electrical circuits.

questions.question: Metals are generally ____ conductors of heat and electricity.
questions.explanation: Metals have free electrons that move easily, making them good conductors of both heat and electricity.

questions.question: The shiny appearance of a freshly cut metal surface is called:
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shiny appearance of metals. Gold, silver, and copper have a characteristic metallic lustre.

questions.question: Which of these is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Sulphur is a non-metal. It is a yellow solid that does not conduct electricity and lacks metallic lustre.

questions.question: Non-metals are generally ____ conductors of electricity.
questions.explanation: Most non-metals are poor conductors (insulators) of electricity. Graphite (a form of carbon) is an exception.

questions.question: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Silver is the best conductor of electricity among all metals, though copper is more commonly used due to cost.

questions.question: The property by which metals produce a ringing sound when struck is called:
questions.explanation: Sonority is the property of metals to produce a ringing sound when hit. School bells are made of metals for this reason.

questions.question: Mercury is a metal that is:
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature. It is used in thermometers.

questions.question: Non-metals are generally:
options: Brittle and dull (except iodine and graphite)
questions.explanation: Non-metals are usually brittle (break easily), non-lustrous, and poor conductors. Iodine and graphite are exceptions.

questions.question: Which of these is the only non-metal that is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only non-metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature. It is a reddish-brown liquid.

questions.question: Aluminium is used to make cooking utensils because it:
options: Has low density and good thermal conductivity
questions.explanation: Aluminium is lightweight (low density) and conducts heat well, making it ideal for cooking utensils.

questions.question: Which form of carbon is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite, a form of carbon (non-metal), is a good conductor of electricity due to its layered structure with free electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following physical properties is common to most metals?
questions.explanation: Most metals have high density (they are heavy for their size), though there are exceptions like sodium and potassium.

questions.question: Iron is used in making bridges and buildings because it has:
questions.explanation: Iron is very strong and hard, making it useful for construction. However, it rusts and is often used as steel alloy.
